accepted is coherent only with highest_completed_stage accepted, no failed applicable validator, refusal_state none, failure_category null, and required accepted artifact hashes.

attempt_state_coherence_validator_v1 is a final nonrecursive harness-integrity check; it is not an input to its own state or to completion of deterministic_validators_passed.

Run-level retry selection may not rewrite any earlier attempt ledger, outcome, stage, disposition, failure, refusal, validator, or hash field.

Every attempt with a canonical non-streaming response body, completed semantic stream, or native pre-SDK raw byte surface records raw_provider_response_hash; optional wire bytes, native-object hashes, and raw_response_unavailable_reason never substitute for it.

HTTP transfer framing is removed before Content-Encoding decoding, and neither Content-Encoding nor arbitrary network chunk boundaries can change raw_provider_response_hash for identical canonical parser bytes.
A partial or ambiguously terminated stream never becomes an accepted semantic result.

No SDK or native-object path is eligible unless canonical raw-byte capture and complete lossless equivalence against an independent pre-SDK strict reference, or a separately frozen authoritative guarantee covering every required property, are demonstrated without circular or self-attested evidence.

Every provider semantic number retains its exact RFC 8259 lexeme through exact decimal parsing and must pass semantic_numeric_domain_policy_v1 before any normative JCS semantic hash or canonical schema validation is produced.

Negative zero, binary64 overflow to non-finite, nonzero underflow to zero, and an exact-decimal change through the RFC 8785 representation fail as failed_canonical_validation with a safe application-owned numeric reason and no accepted semantic hash.

Accepted semantic numeric equality, JSON Schema integer semantics, and range comparisons use exact accepted mathematical decimal values; booleans never qualify as numbers or integers and strings are never coerced to numbers.

Native-object numeric equivalence is proven only by independently admitting and comparing raw/reference and candidate values under semantic_numeric_domain_policy_v1; out-of-domain values cannot become equal through SDK or binary64 rounding.
No transport, SDK, adapter, or native structured transformation may hide, rename, coerce, normalize, or suppress provider-produced semantic fields before H3 and additionalProperties validation.
